title: Middleware Composition
description: Learn how to compose multiple middleware and understand the applyMiddleware API.

data.text: In real applications you rarely use just one piece of middleware. You might combine a logger, an analytics tracker, and an async middleware like Thunk. Understanding how these pieces compose lets you build a robust, layered side-effect pipeline.

Every middleware wraps `dispatch` in a chain. When you compose multiple middleware, the result is a nested function call. The first middleware in the array sits closest to the call site, and each one calls `next(action)` to pass control to the next.

data.text: In modern Redux, you compose middleware inside `configureStore` using the `middleware` option. The `getDefaultMiddleware` helper returns the default set (thunk, serializable check, immutable check), and you can `concat` your own custom middleware.

data.title: applyMiddleware
Order Matters
data.text: The order in which you list middleware determines the order they run. Place cross-cutting concerns like logging first so they see every action. Place thunks or sagas last so they can wrap async behavior.

terms.definition: A sequence of processing steps where the output of one becomes the input of the next.
A Redux store enhancer that lets you compose multiple middleware into a single dispatch chain.
A utility that combines multiple functions into one, calling each in sequence with the result of the previous.

cards.title: configureStore (RTK)
cards.description: Modern approach. Use getDefaultMiddleware().concat(...) to add your own.

cards.title: applyMiddleware (Classic)
cards.description: Classic approach. Use createStore(reducer, applyMiddleware(a, b, c)).

data.title: Build a Middleware Stack
data.description: Compose three pieces of middleware in a single Redux Toolkit store and observe the order they run.
steps: Write a logger middleware that prints the action type and the previous and next state
Write a timing middleware that measures how long the dispatch takes
Write a crash reporter that catches any errors thrown by next(action)
Compose all three in configureStore using getDefaultMiddleware().concat(...)
Dispatch a few actions and confirm the order matches the order you composed them
data.expectedOutcome: You can build a small middleware stack, understand the order in which middleware runs, and know how to add custom middleware to a Redux Toolkit store.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Middleware form a nested pipeline around dispatch
configureStore lets you compose middleware with getDefaultMiddleware().concat()
Order matters: the first middleware in the array runs first
Always place cross-cutting concerns like logging early in the chain
applyMiddleware is the classic API still found in older code
data.takeaway: Composing middleware lets you build a clean, layered side-effect pipeline for your Redux app.
